newsitem.title: CHINA: Plan to float Chinese warship faces fund shortage.
newsitem.headline: Plan to float Chinese warship faces fund shortage.

text.p: A plan to raise a famed Chinese warship from its watery grave in central China is badly short of funds, the China Daily said on Tuesday.

Authorities in Hubei province had raised just 11 million yuan ($1.3 million) of the 100 million yuan ($12 million) needed to salvage the cruiser "Chungshan", which was sunk in an attack by Japanese warplanes in 1938, the newspaper said.
Provincial vice-governor Li Daqiang appealed to Chinese at home and overseas to donate money.
"It is really difficult for us to carry on with so large a project relying only on financial allocations by the local government," the paper quoted Li as saying.
Chungshan is the formal name of Sun Yat-sen, considered to be the father of modern China for his role in the 1911 revolution that toppled the nation's last dynasty.
Refloating work is scheduled to begin on November 12, the 130th anniversary of his birth.
The project also aims to make the ship seaworthy and to build a museum detailing its history, the newspaper said.
The 62-metre long (203-foot) cruiser, built in Japan in 1913, was sunk near Wuhan, an industrial city that was a flashpan of Sun's revolution.

The ship suffered further damage in 1958 at the start of the catastrophic Great Leap Forward when people tore off chunks of the cruiser's hull as part of a national drive to boost steel production, the newspaper said.
